newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says Quintana to invest $40 mln in oil block.
newsitem.headline: Peru says Quintana to invest $40 mln in oil block.

text.p: U.S. firm Quintana Minerals Corp will invest an estimated $40 million to explore and develop oil block 81 in a contract signed last week with the government, state-run Perupetro said Tuesday.

Under the terms of the contract, Quintana will pay a cash royalty on any oil and gas it produces from the 982,000 hectare area in the central Peruvian jungle, Perupetro said in a statement, without giving more details.
Quintana Minerals, based in Houston, has exploration and production projects in the United States, Argentina and Russia and produced an average of 26,000 barrels per day of oil, Perupetro said.
In Peru, the firm also has a 20 percent stake in a joint venture with Argentina's YPF to explore and develop oil block 50, Perupetro, the state oil company Petroperu's licensing arm, added.
This year, the government has signed 11 exploration and development contracts, including one, earlier this week, with the Phillips Petroleum Ltd.
The government has said it hopes to sign a further three contracts before the end of the year, and eight more in 1997.

Of the government's 36 current oil contracts with private companies, 21 are at the exploration stage and 15 are producing oil. The contracts cover a total area of more than 20 million hectares, according to Perupetro.

The government has said Perupetro is also close to signing contracts involving Peruvian miner Buenaventura, oil giants Royal Dutch/Shell Mobil Corp, Atlantic Richfield Co, and Argentina's Pluspetrol Corp.
((-- Saul Hudson, Lima newsroom, 511 221-2134)) REUTER AC SH
